Directed by Dr. Drago Chloupek and shot by Aleksandar Gerasimov, it captures cities, villages, and diverse communities—Albanians, Serbs, Turks, Roma, and Jews—with lasting historical depth.

In a remote forest in north-west Germany, an urban combat facility is used to train British soldiers before deployment in Northern Ireland. A spokesperson for the Irish underground terrorist organisation, the IRA, explains their response.

Tingëllimë is a conceptual film focused on the idea of what makes a home. It raises questions about something we experience every day but rarely stop to reflect on deeply. Is it the people, the walls, or something else that truly makes a house a home?

Chatila and Reda are saving to pay for fake passports to get out of Athens. But when Reda loses their hard-earned cash to his dangerous drug addiction, Chatila hatches an extreme plan, which involves them posing as smugglers and taking hostages in an effort to get him and his best friend out of their hopeless environment before it is too late.

In pandemic-stricken Cuba, Landi hunts crocodiles by hand in the Zapata marshes to feed his family. His wife Mercedes gathers charcoal and cares for their autistic son. As days pass with no word from Landi, fear grows. When he finally returns, their cycle of survival, absence, and silence continues.

German director Wim Wenders travels to Tokyo to explore the world of one of his cinematic heroes, Japanese celebrated film director Yasujirō Ozu. Sequences of Wenders’ view of Japan alternate with encounters and conversations with the crew and cast members of Ozu’s films.

Discover the story of the first ski-mountaineering traverse of the Sharr Massif: an authentic adventure across the lesser-known peaks of the Balkans on the border between Kosovo and Macedonia. Through the lens of skiing, the film reveals the rugged beauty and timeless allure of a region still unexplored in its winter guise, offering a profound contrast to the nearby bustling Alps.

Two Times in One Space by Ivan Ladislav Galeta is an experimental black-and-white film based on Nikola Stojanović’s 1968 single-shot In the Kitchen. In 1984, Galeta merged two delayed projections into one, creating a staggered visual narrative. The film contrasts family life with a balcony love scene, exploring spatial perception, cinematic illusion, and the potential of analog techniques to alter reality. It challenges viewers to engage with multiple layers of meaning simultaneously.

Archive footage and animation recreate New York City, August 13–15, 1965, centered on The Beatles’ iconic Shea Stadium concert. Interwoven with events like the World’s Fair and Watts riots, the film evokes the era’s spirit and fading innocence. A haunting audiovisual time capsule that summons vanished youth and shared memory.

Through rare and long-forgotten footage, this documentary uncovers the hidden machinery of Alfredo Stroessner's dictatorship in Paraguay—one of history's longest-running regimes. From propaganda to international broadcasts, the film exposes how media shaped power, controlled memory, and built a legacy that still lingers today.

Pedro travels for the first time in one of the vans leading a group of workers to France. While, for the others, this is another work trip, each kilometer brings Pedro closer to a place that seduces him: the colossal mountains of the Alps.

Traversing the Andean Highlands, the Atacama Desert, and the coastal cliffs on the way to Iquique’s marginalized settlements and makeshift communities, UNWELCOMED unveils — through a choral narrative — the harsh reality of the Venezuelan migration crisis in Latin America, alongside the cultural clash and rising radicalization in northern Chile.

The girls of the soccer club FFC Wacker are fighting for the championship title in the Bayernliga. During a night-time training session, their dream of becoming professional players becomes reality for a brief moment.

Mladen Stilinović’s Walls, Coats, Shadows is a color film in three parts, focusing on gray walls, dark-toned coats, and fleeting shadows. Though shot in color, the imagery feels monochrome, evoking “gray socialism.” With irony and wit, the film explores absence, uniformity, and fleeting presence, key themes in Stilinović’s work. By omitting faces, he emphasizes anonymity and individual traces within collective life, using structuralist methods to reflect on everyday existence.

Kaylee Hord, a 17-year-old prank video influencer, is the newest member of a popular TikTok content house where she struggles to fit in and pay the rent. But when a new and intense friendship offers the chance of viral fame, Kaylee learns how far she'll go to belong.
The story of Hoa Thi Le and Hue Nguyen Che, who, in 1975, after fleeing the Vietnam War by boat and docking in the Philippines, were utilized as background extras in the filming of APOCALYPSE NOW.

A Tamil woman loses her son to a supernatural entity plaguing her community in a war-torn village in Northern Sri Lanka. Intertwining with her journey are real-life testimonies with women whose family members vanished at the hands of military forces during the civil war.

Yuck! Couples kissing on the mouth is gross. And the worst is, you can't miss them: when people are about to kiss, their lips become all pink and shiny. Léo laughs at them, just like all the kids at the summer camp. But he has a secret he won't tell his friends: when he thinks about little Lucie, his mouth starts to glisten.

Tayfun, an undertaker for the Belgian-Turkish community, must help families decide where their loved ones should be buried. Through his wry humour and daily negotiations, 2m² reveals the mix of belonging, bureaucracy and small absurdities that shape life between two homelands.

3 Generations tells the story of Zadife, a woman whose unwavering faith sustains her through diaspora, war, loss and resilience. Structured in four chapters, the film follows her spiritual journey, her family’s escape from Kosovo during the 1999 war, memories of a childhood shaped by a deeply religious father, and her life as a widow raising five children. Through family archives and Albanian traditions, the film celebrates faith, perseverance and community strength in the face of adversity.

Atlanta plans to build Cop City, the largest police training center in the United States, threatening a vital urban forest. Forest defenders occupy the land, disrupting construction for over a year. After police raid the forest and kill an activist, Tortuguita, a resistance movement erupts throughout the city. A City in the Forest captures a reckoning over environmental justice, police militarization, and democracy.

films.t: A Few Things Happening By a River
films.ot: Algumas Coisas Que Acontecem Ao Lado De Um Rio
films.syn: A group of teenagers floats down the river, pretending to be dead for social media. One of them drifts away.

films.t: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
films.syn: At 16, Soraya, a gifted Afghan sculptor and illustrator living in Iran, dreams of joining her mother in Austria. Filmed remotely over five years by Mehrdad Oskouei using footage Soraya shot herself, the documentary follows her escape attempts, abusive marriage, and artistic journey. Through drawings, sculptures, and animations, Soraya transforms fear, hope, and resilience into powerful acts of self-expression.

From the Second World War to the Algerian War, from the benches of IDHEC to the guerrillas of the FAR in Guatemala, and through Castro–Guevara-era Cuba, A life, a manifesto traces the extraordinary destiny of Michele Firk — a woman passionate about cinema and revolution, a free lover, completely liberated from the conventions of her time.

A Long Goodbye tells the story of Ida, a 72-year-old pianist living with dementia. In this animated, interactive VR experience, we walk in Ida’s shoes. We experience a day in her life, as her reality is fading. The apartment, where she spent a lifetime with her beloved husband Daniel, first feels empty and undefined. When we interact with objects and play the tape recordings of her husband, her playful world gradually comes to life, as if drawn in paint before our eyes.

Ahmed, a young man living in a workers' city on Egypt’s edge, who recently graduated from film school and gets a job in the capital, Cairo. Meanwhile, his close friend wants to emigrate abroad. Ahmed’s thoughts about starting his future in a new city force him to confront the past of his decaying hometown, which pushes him to leave, while he cannot bring himself to leave his mother alone.

Adem works on a construction site in Germany. While he lays the foundations for the lives of others, something within him begins to fracture. Amid the relentless rhythm of undocumented labor, he is haunted by the presence of a lost connection. As someone else’s memories slowly become his own, he searches for a way to send them back to Kosovo.

Training, Take-Off, Grand Prix. Legacy is one of the most valuable and celebrated horses in show jumping. In pursuit of victories, she is flown between competition venues across the globe. Air Horse One follows Legacy on her long journeys in the business class of equine air travel.
A teenager joins a singing competition for a chance to move to the city, while hiding his true voice in a sinister way.

Two Albanian construction workers in Finland mistake panic attacks for heart disease and begin self-diagnosing and self-medicating with unwavering confidence. As pride overrides reason, their improvised treatment spirals — landing them together in the emergency room.

films.t: All The Birds Will Be Gone
films.syn: During the last trip before college with her two best friends, Hui finds herself with an unexpected heartbreak.

films.t: Always wanted to be God, never wanted to do good
films.syn: At the summits of Swiss mountains, Christian crosses stand tall. In the cities, billboards displaying Bible verses occupy public space. I have never felt comfortable with the presence of these religious symbols. In 2009, mountain guide Patrick Bussard sawed down a cross in the Fribourg Alps; he was severely punished by the courts.

In 1996, a Brazilian official and a Swedish journalist ventured into the Amazon to document the isolated Korubo people caught in escalating land conflicts. Initially hailed as unique images from a hidden world, the footage now warrants re-examination. Uncovering the costs of “discovery,” the film confronts the colonial legacy and exposes the long-term repercussions for the Korubo.

AMERICAN DOCTOR is a vérité documentary following three prominent physicians–Palestinian, Jewish and Zoroastrian—friends who couldn’t be more different but are bound by the shared oath to save lives. Dr. Thaer Ahmad is measured and strategic, Dr. Mark Perlmutter is blunt and wears his heart on his sleeve, and Dr. Feroze Sidhwa is media-savvy and prolific. Filmed in unfolding, on-the-ground scenes, the story follows them from a Gazan hospital under siege, to the halls of Congress. Together they fight to keep a promise to their Palestinian colleagues and patients, to continue the struggle where it matters most: the United States.

Agronomist, poet, utopian thinker, and revolutionary... Often referred to as the African Che Guevara, Cabral led the anti-colonial movement in Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde against Portuguese colonialism until his murder in 1973. Human rights, utopias, interracial love, ambition, war, and betrayal are the ingredients of this free portrait crafted with archival images and an imaginary diary in 16mm film. A cinematic documentary that expresses all the modernity of Cabral's world vision.

Haunted by questions of disappearance, loss, and revolutionary struggle, An Impossible Address continues Sanzgiri’s examination of the life of Sita Valles and the bonds of solidarity that developed between India and Africa against the Portuguese empire. Combining 16 mm film with digital animation, hand processing, and 3D scanning, the film is a kaleidoscopic and sonically vibrant experimental personal essay shot across Angola, Goa, and Portugal.

Inspired by the 1980 vinyl record Rhymes and Songs for OPEC, this essay film uses songs and rare archival footage to reconsider oil not as a commodity, but as a political force that supported Palestinian liberation and strengthened Pan-Arab solidarity in the 1960s and 1970s. The film is the final chapter in filmmaker Sanaz Sohrabi’s trilogy examining the relationship between image-making, archival technologies, and the visual cultures of resource extraction in Iran and West Asia.

In Prishtina, Kosovo, Genc, an unemployed fringe blogger devoted to anonymous research, lives with his partner Bora, a US Embassy worker with unfulfilled dreams of writing. While Genc holds on to hopes for a brighter future, Bora, burdened by financial strain and fed up with his detachment, storms out after a heated argument. Now he must find where she’s gone before it’s too late for them.

A child is pulled up by the ski lift bar, another time it cannot open the door anymore after going to the toilet and yet another time it is too slow when leaving the bus and drives away without its mother. A short episodic film about fears we suffer from as children and we can smile about as adults.
A narrator tells about his beautiful life, but a piece of music interrupts him from time to time, forcing him to start over, denying himself and revealing an increasingly bitter truth.

In the summer of 1994, in a small pasture in Argentina, a group of children gather to play soccer under the warm sun of the siesta hour. However, what begins as another day of fun will soon become a memory.

films.t: Arabesques on the Theme of Pirosmani
films.syn: A documentary about the great, but marginal Georgian artist Niko Pirosmani. Using footage of the details and themes of Pirosmani's colorful paintings, Parajanov creates a captivating and mysterious portrait of Georgia.
Filmed in a derelict suburban shopping mall, the film features an ensemble of disabled and non-disabled dancers and is a re-imagination of a performance of the same title by Stopgap Dance Company.

films.t: As the Spring Arrives, Water Recalls the Nomads
films.syn: A heterogeneous group of shepherds travels through the Çukurova valley in Turkey, following in the footsteps of their nomadic ancestors. Between archives and imaginary correspondence, the film becomes an echo of the memory and disappearance of pastoral ecosystems.

On the beach, in the middle of the night, Esther gazes at the stars. Beside her, a strange creature, half-fish, half-human, watches her and tries to catch her attention. To do so, it brings her several objects. Finally realising the extent of her fascination with the stars, the fish ends up bringing her a starfish. Its attempts fail, however, as Esther keeps her eyes fixed on her telescope. Resigned, the creature dives back down to the bottom of the water. Splashed by the creature’s plunge, Esther finally turns her head.

Baby Gun is a documentary and fiction hybrid short film. The film is set during the annual holiday of Karabash in Prizeren, Kosovo. The tradition celebrates the begging of summer and is discussed due to its pagan origins. Imitaiton rifles and guns are often bought for young boys during the celebration. The film simulates the atmosphere of a battlefield among various groups. The children engage in combat while playing in the city park. Their actions and attention is isolated from the faraway lives and problems of contemporary adulthood surrounding them. The film explores collective memory, generational trauma, and masculinity in societies shaped by recent violence, conflict, and war.
Is there any connection between sunglasses, high school friends and nicknames? And could it have something to do with sombreros?
Two girls dream of watching the famous Bambi cartoon at the cinema. But when the show is sold out, they turn the riverside into their very own cinema.

Verdun, 1916. At the dawn of a battle, a telephone operator is called into a trench to repair the line of a command post. He is just twenty years old, he lost his right ear in an explosion, and the left is not much better. He doesn't even have a gun, his name is Julien, and he will be drawn into the violence and absurdity of war.

Berna, a young woman weighed down by an unspoken trauma, moves through the neon-lit streets of Prishtina, haunted by a menacing specter of her past. As she attempts to navigate her bleak existence, a series of violent encounters forces her to confront her deepest fears, culminating in a moment of brutal catharsis.

films.t: Better Go Mad in the Wild
films.syn: Franta and Ondra, wilderness twins, face a fractured bond as Franta yearns for adventure while Ondra desires stability. Their harmonious life unravels, leading to a poignant tale of separation, reconciliation, and possible reunion, exploring what remains when their shared world crumbles.

From besieged Aleppo to the confines of a London newsroom, Lebanese journalist Janay Boulos and Syrian activist /cameraman Abd Alkader Habak retrace their love story, using their vast personal archives stretching over 13 years of revolutions, war and exile. Can their love survive distance, danger, and differences?

Black Girl (1966), the feature debut of acclaimed Senegalese filmmaker and novelist Ousmane Sembène, follows a young Senegalese woman who moves to France to work for a wealthy white couple, only to find herself trapped in a life of isolation and exploitation. Featuring a powerful performance by Mbissine Thérèse Diop, the film is both a moving human drama and a sharp critique of colonialism, widely regarded as a landmark of African cinema. Restored by Cineteca di Bologna/ L’Immagine Ritrovata laboratory, in association with the Sembène Estate, Institut National de l’Audiovisuel, INA, Eclair laboratories and the Centre National de Cinématographie. Restoration funded by The Film Foundation’s World Cinema Project.

In 1968, Agnès Varda directed Huey and Black Panthers , documentaries inspired by her time in California. Offering a firsthand look at the Black Panther movement, the films challenge media portrayals of the group as a threat. Moving from observation to political commentary, Varda highlights the Panthers’ activism, public image and impact on Oakland’s African American community while documenting a pivotal moment in U.S. history.

Manhattan, 1983. Tasked with helping her father run his deli on the night of its 24/7 opening, an unassertive teenager distracts herself with dreams of superstardom, while a few blocks away her idol, David Bowie, embarks on his first tour in five years.

The documentary, discovered on a VHS tape, recounts, through the author's own experience, the rebellion of the Mk3 service droids against human hegemony. This unprecedented work presents history from the perspective of those who endured it, restoring dignity and humanity to androids, often relegated to a state of subordination. The hopes, dreams, and fears of the men of steel are gathered in this archive of the future, revealing lesser-known aspects of the "Silicon Rebellion."

With a visual background containing images of an abandoned building, Albin, the only child in a family of three, shares his feelings on having his extended family abroad through a mixture of narration and conversation with his parents.

“Butterfly” was created in collaboration with the residents of the “Mladost” Children’s Home in Bijela, where no child has continued their education after leaving. Through the filmmaking process, 15 children learned about acting and film, but their real-life stories overpowered the script. The film becomes an honest encounter with reality, where a lesson in cinema grows into a lesson in life - love as the only means of resistance.

Hospitals are cold, unforgiving places. Especially for children who spend weeks or months within their walls, a single day can feel like a year. Every week, Paco, a retired banker, puts on a red nose and walks the halls of the children's ward at Vall d'Hebron Hospital in Barcelona. For a moment, routines break and rooms fill with laughter, offering the children a brief escape from fear and boredom alike. What remains are smiles, silence — and a butterfly.

Sam, a grumpy raccoon is stuck sharing a cell with Bob, a sweet but dim manatee. In their chaotic jailbreak Sam’s hardened edges soften as Bob’s loyalty shines. Will they escape? Maybe. But together, they’ve already cracked something bigger: trust.

‘Celtic Utopia’ unravels modern Irish history and introduces us to a refreshingly broad cast of characters, including pierced punks, rappers, and ravers, who come together to revive and reinterpret the classic folk music tradition with humor and renewed indignation. Prominent groups such as The Mary Wallopers and Lankum deliver sharp punchlines and even sharper songs, of which there are fortunately plenty in the film.

Cameroon on the brink of independence. The Dalens’ live in a small town, run by the French Administration. Marc, the father, is hardly ever home. Aimée, the mother spends most of her days in her yard, gardening. France is their daughter, and she just keeps to what is going on, together with Protée, the black boy running the house, and her best friend.Their peaceful lives are disrupted when an airplane makes a forced landing on their property.

Christiania chronicles over 50 years of the famous Copenhagen freetown, one of the world’s most radical social experiments. Through remarkable archival footage, director Karl Friis Forchhammer traces its journey from a 1971 occupation of abandoned barracks to a unique community shaped by freedom, creativity, conflict, drugs, biker gangs, and political struggles. A vivid portrait of a place constantly redefining itself while fighting to survive.

In the remote Siberian Arctic, an Indigenous Sakha scientist descends into the depths of the melting permafrost. Searching for an ancient creature, he makes his way through the dangerous caves to the mythical realm of the Underworld.

Daniel didn’t hear his 16-year-old son, Chris, slip out of the house that early morning. He didn’t know what pulled him onto a bridge over the boisterous Vistula River in Warsaw—only that it was the last place he was seen. A rotating CCTV camera captured him there, and then, between turns, he vanished, leaving two possibilities: that he went into the river, or made it off the bridge unseen. Since that moment, Daniel and his wife, Agnieszka, have lived suspended between desperate hope and paralyzing fear.

War experienced through eyes of a child. Masculinity, cinema, loss. Zulfikar Filandra's newest film can be understood as his most minimal work, all footage is sourced except three personal photographs donated by his family - but again the final cinematic entity delivers timeless emotional depth and punch while dancing around the timeless themes of war and masculinity and the effect of these images on actual - lived - experienced - survived - reality.

Two young brothers live on the outskirts of Mexico City. Mario wakes up with no memories from his previous life. Adrift, he meets Lazarus, who teaches him how to enter other people's bodies through vast holes in the Earth. In the darkness of subterranean cavities, Mario’s memories fill his mind like dreams. The history of the land runs through his corporality. The space he passes through is distorted and his skin begins to crack along with the landscape.

Years after their imprisonment, the director gathers his close friends to return to fragments of a past that never fully passed. Sitting together, they look at images and moments once sealed away, not to reconstruct events, but to sense what still lingers. As memories surface through scars, dreams, humor, and silence, the film traces a shared attempt to make space for one another, and observes how trauma lives on in the body and in everyday life. Some images return clearly; others remain unstable, fading or breaking apart. Compact Disc stays with them—searching for what might emerge when unspeakable moments are allowed to exist, held collectively, without demand for resolution.
Bia, a Census worker, sets out on a relentless quest to find the last inhabitant of a remote village, in the hope of preventing it from becoming a mere statistical value, sunk into oblivion.

In an intimate conversation with her daughter and granddaughter, a grandmother reflects on a lifetime shaped by crochet and needlework. As she recalls learning the craft from her sister and receiving her first needle from her father, her memories unfold into a story of love, resilience, and loss. Through the threads of handmade doilies, Kujtimet Përmes Tenteneve reveals how family history and memory are passed from one generation of women to the next.
During their flight from war, eighteen year old Uka and his family make a final stop to take Ema, the girl he loves. She waits for them like a bride ready to exchange rings, but one ring is missing.

In the English countryside, two neighbours named Derek clash over the future of the land. One is an intensive dairy farmer committed to industrial food production; the other is rewilding his farm, restoring habitats and reintroducing native species. As ponds are dug, animals return and tensions rise, their often humorous feud becomes a story about competing visions of nature, farming and the landscape.

Inside a medical training facility, one of the “Da-Vinci” surgical robots gains autonomy and self-awareness. It starts wandering around the building and discovers a hybrid space where clinical progress blurs with echoes of warfare. Created by the U.S. Army in the 1980s, Da-vinci’s initial purpose was to operate on wounded soldiers in remote battlefields. The film reflects upon the boundary between healing and killing: being a tool of care as well as a posthuman weapon of precision.

What happens when a documentary fails to become the film it set out to be? During DokuFest’s Re:Connect program in Prizren, Kosovo, director Max Haller sets out to film Diti, a local hairdresser who dreams of building a future in Switzerland. But technical mishaps, constant interruptions, and a chaotic one-day shoot derail the original plan. Forced to improvise, the film transforms into a playful hybrid of documentary, behind the scenes diary, and mockumentary, where the filmmaking process itself becomes the story told through the perspective of an unexpected narrator: a boom michrophone.

Do You Love Me is a playful and personal journey through Lebanon’s audiovisual memory, composed entirely of archival footage. It is a love letter to Beirut, spanning 70 years of film, TV, home videos, and photography, exploring the Lebanese collective psyche – marked by joy and intimacy, destruction and loss. Through the eyes of citizens, filmmakers and artists, the film reconstructs a fragmented history in a country without a national archive, celebrating creative expression as both resistance, renewal and a way to preserve memory.

This is the story of Mirela, a Bosnian woman who lives in Italy but who arrived with a humanitarian convoy during the 1992 siege of Sarajevo when she was only 10 years old. It is also the story of her return to Sarajevo after a long time as she searches for her former schoolmates from the Institute where she grew up. She also searches for her mother who gave her up to the Institute, she searches for Bosnia, her mother-land and finally, she searches for herself. The year 2026 marks the 30th anniversary of the end of the siege of Sarajevo, adding a significant layer of contemporary relevance to Mirela's story.

An intimate portrait of a celebrated boundary pushing artist who has given everything for his art. As the border between reality and performance blurs, the shifting relationship between filmmaker and subject calls into question who is actually making the film.

films.t: Dragica, Danica, Duška / or / When Zora, the Goddess of Dawn, Opens the Gates of Heaven for Sun to Emerge
films.syn: Danica, Dragica, Duška revolves around Zora, the Slavic goddess of dawn. Zora either appears as one figure or as a triad of sisters representing sunrise, noon, and sunset— the past, present, and future. Together, they are guardians of time. The three grandmothers of the artist give their title to the work. The goddess is said to dwell in the Palace of the Sun, reigning over the cosmos. In moments of battle, she is believed to lower her veil, shielding favored warriors from harm.
A woman's collapse amid urban ruins sparks an exploration of humanity's connection to physical spaces and a city's resilience in the face of mortality.

films.t: Elegy for the Forgotten, on an Endless War
films.ot: مرثیه‌ای برای فراموش‌شدگان، در باب جنگی بی‌پایان
films.syn: Almost 40 years since the Iran-Iraq War, destruction has come back to Iran, on the heels of an unprecedented revolt in January 2026, which ended with the government killing thousands of Iranians on the streets. As Israeli and American bombs began falling, images of the war were tightly controlled by the regime. Who produces the images and who controls the narrative in a complex political game that seems to never end? What do archives tell us about the present moment?

Directed by award-winning and emerging filmmakers from around the world, ELEMENTAL is a thought-provoking series of short documentaries that explore our lives through the elements of the periodic table. There are as many stories about how the elements touch our lives as there are creative ways to portray them, and the collection champions films from across the wide spectrum of creative documentary approaches.
A data-driven, nonfiction short film documenting the surge of U.S. incidents where law enforcement has targeted journalists since May 25, 2020.
Ethel discovers clothes of her late mother and embarks on a search to unearth memories. The child attempts to understand her mother’s passion. A tale of letting go and growing up.

A lively kid named „O” is very curious and busy discovering the world around. Despite all the obstacles O manages to gather some personal experiences and to gain some new skills. Will they prove useful? A short story told from a child’s perspective. For parents. And little humans.

Lumbardhi Experimental Ensemble returns with its first full one-hour performance, combining original live music with four documentary and archival films from Kosovo (1933–1976). The programme features some of the earliest surviving moving images from Kosovo, anthropological documentaries, portraits of urban and rural life, and newly rediscovered materials from the Lumbardhi Cinema archive. Developed during a week-long workshop, the ensemble creates a new audio-visual experience that brings these films into dialogue with contemporary live performance. - City of Beauty and Resources – Zvonko Saksida (1972), 17 min - Kroz Naše Kosovo - Drago Chloupek (1933), 25 min - 117 – Besim Sahatçiu (1976), 19 min - Pehlivanët - Besim Sahatçiu (1975), 14 min

What remains of a place once everyone has left? A daughter walks through the village her father left decades ago. Filmed by hand, the images tremble like memory itself. She searches for a language to hold what remains.

Lost in her fears and fantasies, a young woman writes in a notebook. A young man finds this notebook on a train. Suddenly, they find themselves in the heart of a forest, in a nocturnal reality where dreams come to life.

Found footage recorded on March 12, 1998, in Germany, documenting Agron and Fitnete as they receive their marriage papers. Surrounded by family, they record heartfelt congratulations and greetings intended for loved ones back in Kosova. What begins as a celebratory message, slowly shifts into a moment marked by uncertainty and concern about Kosova.
Mireille promises Johnny the big screen, dragging him to an audition whose rules only she truly knows.

As wildfires rage, seas rise, storms intensify and landscapes shift, nature sends both warnings and guidance. FIRE, WATER, EARTH, AIR follows four Nordic communities building collective resilience in response to climate change. Blending everyday life with science, the film explores how enduring connections with nature and one another can help us navigate an uncertain future.
In the tough neighbourhood of Tepito, a young boy chases the great Mexican dream: to become a boxing champion.

On a lonely night, a girl searching for her missing dog is transported to a magical world, where she reunites with her friend in an unexpected form. As she explores this whimsical realm, she confronts memories from her life.

In 1988, Afghanistan’s first and only astronaut, Abdul Ahad Momand, traveled to space and made Pashto the fourth language ever spoken beyond Earth when he called his mother from orbit. His journey became a brief symbol of hope as Afghanistan descended into turmoil and millions were forced into exile. Blending history with personal reflection, the film explores diaspora, colonial legacies, and the memory of a fractured and silenced nation.

In a hill-side village in Ticino, Rea is on her way to deliver a love letter to her crush. But, before she has the chance to deliver it, it flies away downhill through the town. In a panic, Rea embarks on a breakneck tumble through the village to catch the letter and finally confess her feelings.

In Marseilles, the sale of Skander's barber shop hinges on Juliette's decision, a young Parisian woman. Mehdi, the apprentice, is playing his future on a call from the bank. It's going to be a long day...

Azem, a hotel security guard, drifts through a quiet, uneventful routine. Cut off from his home and family, he finds solace in the stillness of his job, until a brief encounter with a hotel resident unsettles the calm he’s built.

A Wen, 38, a businessman and family man in Barcelona, is also the filmmaker’s brother. Just like in the gangster movies they watched on VHS as kids, he became involved in the gangs of the Chinese community in Spain in his youth. Without judgement or romanticisation, Xisi Sofia Ye Chen observes a man torn between criminal heritage, familial duty and a search for moral clarity, composing an intimate and powerful portrait.

In northern France, Gabin, the youngest of the Jourdel family, finds himself destined to take over his father’s butcher shop. Torn between family loyalty and a desire to break free, his dreams lie elsewhere: to train a contest cow, to become a dog breeder, and to save his mother’s farm from financial ruin. Spanning a decade, GABIN immerses us in this young boy’s world, following his journey from age 8 to 18.

On a remote Adriatic island, abandoned goats roamed freely for forty years, left behind after a failed agricultural project—until they were deemed a problem. Soon, a group of armed men appears, determined to restore the "natural balance." We bear witness to a chilling cull, revealing the unsettling ease with which we justify violence—and how quickly we convince ourselves it’s the only right thing to do.

Sophie Fiennes’s documentary offers an intimate portrait of pop icon Grace Jones, blending electrifying performances with personal moments. Moving between Jamaica, recording studios and stages around the world, the film reveals Jones as artist, mother, daughter and businesswoman. More than a music biography, it captures the bold spirit, creativity and individuality of a performer who continues to defy expectations.
Kazakhstan. Laura and Daur live in an isolated village high in the mountains. Today, Laura will be travelling to the city to give birth.
With a playful associative montage, Parajanov offers an overview of portrait paintings by Hakob Hovnatanyan, the ‘Raphael of Tiflis’.

Mexhidja was one of seven siblings, but only she and her brother Gëzimi remained in Kosovo during the era of guest worker migration and the Kosovo War. As many families left in search of a better future, they stayed behind, facing the difficulties of a country in crisis. In this short documentary, Mexhidja reflects on that time, sharing the emotional weight of separation. Through her memories, past and present intertwine, revealing not only the struggles she endured but also the unspoken feeling

The world is getting hotter, with new peak temperatures every summer. What does this heat do to people? How does it change us? HEAT is a cinematic exploration of heat as a condition and an extreme experience. Focusing on the Persian Gulf as one of the hottest regions on the planet, HEAT paints a panorama of human stories, moods, and survival strategies. It’s a glimpse into a possible future for all of us.

Blending documentary, religious art, music and cinema, this kaleidoscopic film immerses viewers in the life of The Greater Bethany Community Church in South Central Los Angeles. At its center is Bishop Noel Jones, brother of Grace Jones, whose powerful sermons, gospel music and community leadership reveal the faith, energy and spirit of a vibrant congregation.

A crow drops pebbles into a pitcher, coaxing water to rise — an ancient fable that still shimmers with truth. This film follows the mystery and brilliance of corvids, a family of bold songbirds whose intelligence reveals the wonder hidden in the everyday.

films.t: I can't think of anything right now
films.syn: A young man finds himself caught in a state of limbo. Disembodied, he encounters memories he doesn’t recognise and bargains with a presence he doesn’t know. In his attempt to escape this kafkaesque conundrum, he finds himself confronted with an irreversible choice.

films.t: I couldn't draw you a map
films.syn: Through diary fragments, walking records, daily gestures and urban sounds, I couldn't draw you a map proposes an exploration of separation across different levels: political, territorial, emotional. A constellation of landscapes marked by the traces of the past that quietly filter into the everyday.

films.t: I Heard That They Are Not Going To See Each Other Anymore
films.syn: In Taipei’s dreamscape, Tao’s incomprehensible love for Shin drives her to create painful memories. Meanwhile, Melih, burdened with self-blame, longs to connect with the perpetually drunk Ping.

A raw, self-made and deeply personal work, IF PIGEONS TURNED TO GOLD cuts into addiction and intergenerational trauma, capturing several years in the lives of four family members. Pepa, the director, records on an iPhone and tries to understand why their beloved older brother and cousins live unhoused and experience substance addiction. Formally inventive and playful, diaristic footage enters into dialogue with stylised memories, AI-animated photographs and graphic interventions, shaping a plural voice that negotiates with the past. Unsentimentally, the film traces the causes and fallout of addiction, asking where love ends, control begins, and what respect truly demands: to save, or to let go.

films.t: Imagine Me Like a Country of Love
films.syn: Imagine Me Like a Country of Love is the debut film of Yemeni-born artist Thana Faroq, an experimental documentary that explores the emotional and physical landscapes of returning to a homeland transformed by time and prolonged conflict. After leaving Yemen for the Netherlands because of the war and living there for nearly a decade, I returned to a country still fractured, unstable, and bearing the weight of devastation.

A reversed world where women are in power and men take care of the family. Domenico tells his story to his daughter. In a letter, he relives the joy of his daughter's birth and childhood, his dreams of a happy family, and even his sacrifices as a father.
In nature, a couple is a male and a female. Well, not always! A couple is also a female and a female. Or a male and a male. You may not be aware of it, but homosexuality isn't just a human story.

A figure appears from the future — sent from a world in which Cinema no longer exists — to retrieve a copy of a film starring Nora Gregor. Told in the first person by a Japanese director, as if it were a small psycho-geographical diary about the city of Gorizia.

films.t: Into the Jaws of the Ogre
films.syn: I can’t quite grasp the adventurous life of my brother Siavash, so far from my own. While I have just become French and he is about to become American, far from our native Iran, we are searching for common ground.

In a village where people have been disappearing for years, a group of locals join two men to search for Murad, who recently vanished. They explore a local myth about a mysterious creature living under the snow. Their journey will uncover a secret deeper than they could have imagined.

Hana, a talented teenager, is just days away from graduating from high school. While preparing for the next chapter of her life, she is also fighting to achieve her dream of becoming a professional football player. Her father, Sherif, has a different plan for her future and insists that she pursue academic studies instead. As their opposing wills collide, hidden emotional wounds, fear, and unspoken trauma rise to the surface, pushing the family to a breaking point.

Keko the crow and Kiki the hound are the pets of a couple of grandparents in a small village in north-east Italy. Keko is a real nuisance. Kiki, on the other hand, is very well-behaved and discreet by nature. The two animals spend their days squabbling. They are jealous of the attention the grandparents pay to one or other of them. At home, everything seems to be going well between the grandparents until the day a big argument breaks out.

A Syrian academic in Amsterdam receives shocking footage of a massacre of civilians carried out by an unknown army officer. She traces the perpetrator and poses as “Anna” to friend him on Facebook, luring him into a series of revealing calls. This gripping psychological thriller tells the story of their extraordinary relationship, as she confronts one of the world’s most brutal regimes to expose the depths of its chilling crimes.

In kiss kiss beng beng , a cinematic love portrait composed of home videos, photographs, diary entries, audio recordings and interviews, director Ollie Launspach explores the impact of his gender transition on his girlfriend, Sterre. As he attempts to make sense of her emotional world, the chaos within his own mind becomes increasingly apparent.

On a bitter winter night in Harbin, a boy loses his beloved cards. To ease his anger, he turns to mischief as a form of rebellion. But as each act of defiance gives way to the relentless return of violence—like the unending winter wind—he begins to realize he is caught in a cycle he cannot escape.

The film follows the last day of Kesuma, a young Bagan fisherman who lives on a bamboo fishing platform near Krakatoa. After a night with no catch, he tends to his nets, unaware of the disaster about to strike. A massive eruption and tsunami destroy everything, leaving him stranded on a deserted island. Wandering in search of food and water, he traverses barren coasts, lush jungle, and encounters strange life. Seeking refuge in a cave, he descends into a hallucinatory journey through geological eras, lava rivers, and abstraction itself—until an unimaginable climax awaits.

„Migrating Materialistic Mythopoetics“ (Michael Baute on Kukata Miti) Forests have been cleared, trees have been felled, humans are taking revenge on themselves and their environment. The documentary fairy tale Kukata Miti takes the viewer on a cinematographic journey through landscapes of loss in Germany, Indonesia and the DR Congo.

What was supposed to become a feature-length film about the aftermath of WWII in contemporary Kiev, turned into a short collage, based on the remaining footage after all the negatives were destroyed by the authorities.

Pregnant with her first child, director Agnès Varda turned her camera to her immediate surroundings capturing day-to-day life along the Rue Mouffetard. Lacking synch sound and incorporating a number of unconventional techniques, this short work displays Varda’s freestyle approach to filmmaking and its subject matter.

Five friends explore their relationship with the Albanian language within the diaspora in Switzerland. They wander through places of remembrance where identity is forged, and give voice to Albanian culture in places where it is suppressed. Gjuha e diasporës straddles the line between documentary and experiment, serving as an investigation into what happens to the Albanian language as a result of oppression and migration.
A fantastic story involving Clarisse and the disappearance of her friend Lazare and the bronze lion of the Place de Belfort in the 14th arrondissement of Paris.
A journey through personal imagery and broken poetry, tracing grief, complicity, and presence in a world coming apart.
An epistolary film constructed from VHS tapes sent from Srebrenica between 1993 and 1994 by the filmmaker’s father, depicting the mise-en-scène of “normal life” amid the war.

Actress Nora Gregor dies at the age of forty-seven, in her final exile in Santiago de Chile, three weeks after learning of her mother’s death. It is January 20, 1949. A second later she opens her eyes – and finds herself in Gorizia in the year 2025.

In a world of towering mountains, dutiful train conductor Peregrin navigates his train through dangerous terrain like a well-oiled clock. One day, the free-spirited musician Clara smuggles herself into his machine room. Soon, catastrophe strikes, and Clara and Peregrin have to overcome their differences to save the train from derailing.

films.t: Live Experience: A CAGE IN SEARCH OF A NIGHTINGALE by Elvin Brandhi and Daniel Bird
films.syn: Early this year, Bird and Brandhi plundered the archives of Armenian Public radio, transferring Soviet-era sound effects from original magnetic tapes, while making field recordings in mountainous landscapes and crumbling temples, to make an original soundtrack for this unseen material, in dialogue with the composer of the film’s original soundtrack, Tigran Mansurian. An auditory delight not to be missed! Reiterating the live performance, happening on August 9 in Prizren, Daniel Bird and Elvin Brandhi will shed light on the intersection of analogue and digital media at the beginning of the 21st century. This live performance accentuates Sergey Parajanov and Tigran Manusrian work as dictated by the importance of the spirit of place. Furthermore, it is a lens through which the timelessness of the film's visual poetry becomes ever so clear. The programme and the exhibition are supported by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation.

Italy, late 1960s. Two strangers arrive in a village in the South: one is carrying a film camera, the other a gun. As they travel through that desolate land, the two will have an unexpected opportunity to change the course of history.

Bobby spends his days driving between Vienna and Salzburg, picking up passengers and sharing conversations along the way. Soldiers, students, academics, and others reveal stories of identity, work, family, and belonging. As Bobby reflects on aging and a friend in a coma who inspires his journeys, London becomes a quietly political portrait of contemporary Europe. Blending documentary and fiction, it finds humanity, kindness, and connection in the spaces in between.

Every time Louise the crocodile sneezes, she loses part of her brain, until she cannot perform simple tasks and becomes trapped inside her own apartment. She must find a way to rediscover the world before she fades away completely.

A storm rumbles next door. Mr. L'Espérance hopes to inspire gentleness as he crafts a gift for his neighbor. While working, a flow of memories makes their way to the surface. Vivid images and echoes jostle in his mind, distorting and amalgamating forming into unique visuals. He lives again fragments of his childhood as the son of a sailor .

Imprisoned as a teenager for a violent offence, Ryan finds purpose working with sheep on the prison farm. But the order of the inside is a stark contrast to the chaos he finds upon release as his past refuses to go quietly. Magilligan is an intimate portrait of a man caught between two worlds, with more than just his freedom at stake.

Moon travels through a mysterious world free of adults. She meets a sage, and her translator, in a mountain hut, where she tries to understand what is happening. She meets many others who show her different possibilities for living. She observes and moves on into an unknown future.

A special family of moon guardians lives on a tiny island and deals with the ups and downs of their everyday life and of the tide. The film depicts the delicate balance between the characters and the environment in which they live.

Maya feels at home with her family, but her appearance constantly raises questions. Strangers ask why her skin is brown while her family's is white. When a supermarket employee fails to recognize her as part of her family, it hits her hard. But instead of retreating, she writes a song to share her story. MAYA’S SONG is a film about self-acceptance and the longing to be seen—not for the color of one’s skin, but for who one truly is.

The German Government refuses to pay reparations for its occupation of Namibia in the late 19th and early 20th centuries and for the genocide of the indigenous population. Instead, it proposes development cooperation programs that exude disgusting neocolonialism and terrible racism under an air of solidarity - an obvious thing for everyone, except for German officials and nostalgic tourists.

In this intimate video letter, the director addresses her aunt, a victim of femicide years ago, to tell her what it has been like to live and grow up with her absence. From a performance in which she projects the last Facebook message that her aunt sent her, the young filmmaker reconstructs her own story marked by the fear of inhabiting a dangerous country for women and by the complexity of being the only woman within her family.

A memoir of the director’s grandmother. A trip to the Zupa region cultivates knowledge of war, resistance and cultural identity. As she learns more about the past, layer by layer, everything becomes clearer.

Blending verbatim performance and choral music, Mother Company follows a children’s choir amidst an abandoned power plant in Northern Greece, role-playing as generations of workers of this de-industrialised area. A chorus of young voices reflects on environmental catastrophe, public health and economic depravation while a ‘Green Future’ is promised to save them.

Sometimes a journey doesn’t begin with setting out, but with a question. Driven by a feeling he can’t quite put his finger on, Amir returns to a place he calls home, even though he’s never lived there: Prishtinë. What does it feel like to belong? Surrounded by familiar faces, old paths, and new encounters, he quickly realizes that this question cannot be answered in this place.
On the night before a religious procession, a fifteen-year-old encounters a group of teenagers hidden in the dark of the local sports hall.

Gorizia, 1930. Through the gaze of the cameraman of the Fascist Afterwork Club (OND) we see the regime’s marches and the celebration. By imagining the voice of his thoughts, we delve into his insecurities and his surrender to a silent dissent. The images remain, continuing to tell of a time that has yet to pass.

A girl’s long-distance romance with an older Norwegian man promises to pull her and her mother out of their austere life in Cuba, but her dreams are shaken when she realizes he isn’t as idyllic as he seems.

Lost in the middle of a universal internet, visitors wander through a virtual museum, dressed in wacky avatars. In this psychedelic-tinged anticipation documentary, it is through the bewildered gaze of a fish who arrived there by chance while surfing the internet that the filmmakers lift the veil on the visitors' imaginations and their intimate view of art and the museum space.

films.t: Nothing Is Certain – Two Strolls In Gorizia
films.syn: Summer in Gorizia. A couple is about to leave for their holidays. Between empty streets and closed cinemas, it all feels already behind them. Only Paolino remains, drifting through the city, reminiscing about a lost love.

In the ocean, marine life moves among objects left behind by humans. Through clay animation, the film observes an underwater world where living beings and debris coexist in shifting rhythms of adaptation and survival. Without narration or conventional storytelling, it explores how life continues, transforms, and quietly reorganizes itself in shared space, inviting young audiences to observe change through movement and texture.

A time capsule from the underground. NOVA 78 resurrects the electrifying Nova Convention of 1978 featuring never-before-seen footage of William Burroughs, Frank Zappa, Patti Smith, Brion Gysin, Anne Waldman, Laurie Anderson, Merce Cunningham, and many other icons from the restored archive of Howard Brookner reimagined as a cinematic event for today’s audiences by directors Aaron Brookner and Rodrigo Areias.

A polar bear is forced to navigate a human world of tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as its ancient migration collides with modern life. When a sacred predator is branded a nuisance, it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

Omar is a big, soft-bodied circus freak with crab claws for arms. He has always been exploited by Monsieur Jules, a despotic circus director, and has long since resigned himself to his sad fate. But the arrival of Pincette, a mermaid tightrope walker, turns his life upside down, bringing out new feelings in him. Because Omar loves Pincette and Pincette has a crush on him.

Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self.

A sparrow, obsessed with the image of glamorous ostriches, transforms itself through fitness, beauty routines and neck-stretching. But when it finally meets a real ostrich, it learns a simple truth: no matter how hard it tries, a sparrow can never become an ostrich.
Alihan lives in a small village where he knows everyone and all his peers’ nicknames. He helps his father with the household chores and then goes off to play alchiki with his friends.

Out of Nowhere gently explores how preserving alluvial forests, marshes and wetlands can help us face the challenges of an ever angrier, unpredictable climate. Told through the eyes of Anna, a lifelong resident of Hallein, a historic town at the foot of the Austrian Alps, the experience flows from first-hand experience of the devastating floods that hit Europe in 2021 to reveal how reconnecting with nature may be key to protecting ourselves going forward.

films.t: Over Your Cities Grass Will Grow
films.syn: Artist Anselm Kiefer transformed a former silk factory in southern France into a vast artistic landscape of studios, installations, tunnels and monumental structures. Over Your Cities Grass Will Grow takes viewers through this extraordinary estate, offering an immersive look into Kiefer’s creative process and the visionary world of one of contemporary art’s most influential figures.

In the waters of Colombia’s Pacific coast, life is celebrated through a particular kind of song: the Arrullos. This music honors life in a territory marked by violence and armed conflict, where enslaved people once found refuge at the end of colonial rule. In these same waters, each year, thousands of whales arrive from Antarctica to give birth. Pacífico weaves a polyphonic narrative around birth in an aquatic space where body, territory, and memory are deeply intertwined.

Dutch-Afghan filmmaker Dawood Hilmandi returns to confront his estranged father—a former mujahideen fighter turned imam, writer, and poet—in a search for love, forgiveness, and understanding. Moving between Afghanistan, Iran, and the Netherlands, Paikar explores the invisible legacy of war, silence, and inherited trauma. Through an intimate father-son encounter, the film reveals the tenderness that can endure despite years of distance, conflict, and unspoken pain.
The story follows Pankaja, a woman who, along with her daughter Lalli, desperately navigates the city slums and bureaucracy of Bangalore in a quest to locate her missing husband.

In 1991, as Croatia stood on the brink of war, Josip Reihl Kir, the Osijek police chief committed to dialogue and peace, was assassinated. Peacemaker reconstructs the final months of his life through witness testimonies and archival footage, exploring his efforts to prevent the Croatian-Serbian conflict. More than three decades later, key questions about his murder—and those who ordered it—remain unanswered.
Montreal is being completely transformed into a cyberpunk society. When everything collapses, nature reclaims its rights.

PHENOMENA is a psychedelic journey through the universe, guided by a filmmaker whose practical experiments blur the boundaries between art and science. Captured entirely in-camera, without visual effects, the film combines striking imagery with music by Nils Frahm and Rival Consoles. Moving from the subatomic to the cosmic, it explores the forces shaping nature and our connection to the wonders of the universe.
An Iranian man and a French woman stroll around the city of Isfahan, Iran and find that their love is mirrored perfectly in the architecture and mosaics of the city’s mosques.

A shoal of herrings, adopting fantastic formations, roams the vast ocean. When seagulls suddenly attack, one small herring finds itself stranded in a tidal pool. As it searches desperately for a way out, it discovers many other sea creatures here. And now there is no time for fear: only by joining forces can they hope to defend themselves against the hungry seagull.

A personal documentary that, through archival family footage, shows the relationship between me and my grandmother. It follows the experience of slowly losing her as her illness progresses, how I processed it by drawing a portrait of her, using art as a way to cope with grief and preserve our shared memories.
Baon, a little crocodile, have to face the hardest test of all for a young being : grief.

Sleepless from the heat, Sokun leaves his crowded construction dormitory and joins a community of fellow workers living in one of many unfinished high-rises. One such tower becomes the long-awaited luxury home for its first tenant, Seda, who soon feels isolated in the vast gated complex.

Rainboy isn't a common gardener. He plants drops and grows clouds. While working he injures the vain sun. Revenge! The prognosis for the boy is bleak, but he teams up with the clouds and thus manages to brighten the sun's spirits again.

In Remake, filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March. What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by the urge to keep looking, even when there's no clear story left to tell.

In a part of Dublin known as the Liberties - which is also where the Vikings settled 1100 years ago - there is a small tribe of rebel horse owners. And one day a travelling street musician accidentally crashes her van into the wall of one of their urban horse yards – and out comes a horse and a few boys. One of them brings her for a spin with a horse and two-wheeler, and from that day on she’s hooked…

In an abstract and symbolic world where gravity is reversed, a unique bond forms between a grandfather and his grandson. As Saba, the grandfather guides the boy through this surreal reality, a violent storm strikes, tearing one of the ropes anchoring their home - and with it, their life together.

A half-hour photo montage made up of 1500 stills Agnès Varda took while vacationing in Cuba. Described by Varda as \"socialism and cha-cha-cha\", this short film juxtaposes the photos with infectious rhythms of Cuban dance music while dealing with the revolution of Fidel Castro and his crew, its effects on the people and the island's cultural history.

When masked and nameless US Border Patrol agents abduct a man from a residential street in Chicago's Albany Park neighborhood without a warrant, his neighbors attempt to obstruct the vehicle carrying him from leaving their block.

Three teens disguise themselves for the ritual "Skråbock", a local tradition of begging for Christmas leftovers. They visit their neighbors’ houses and are let in with more or less enthusiasm. But the teens hunger for more than food and explore the ritual's limits. Scraps is a road movie by foot about a night that spirals out of control.
Fili, a former political prisoner, hid two notebooks of poems inside the wall of an apartment during the communist era; fifty years later, he returns to the town to search for them.

Between Bern and Kosova, a daughter traces her mother’s memories and her own fragmented sense of home. Through family archives, everyday moments and intimate conversations, SHP(I)JA explores what it means to belong to more than one place and how the idea of “home” is carried, remembered, and reimagined across generations.

In Kowloon City, Hong Kong, a cultural tour begins, tracing the outline of a walled city that no longer exists. But the group slips out of frame soon enough. In its place, a different kind of cultural tour emerges—less about heritage, more about human nature.

One night in downtown Los Angeles, a man hears the call of a cuckoo from his childhood. Seeking the source of the elusive sound, he slips into a dream where the songs of vanished birds uncover what has long been lost and buried in the land and himself.

Bodies, architecture, and ideas age differently while passing together through time. Sonja Vukićević (73), a dancer and choreographer from Belgrade, is known for her anti-Milošević activism and her monumental solo at the final Youth Day celebration in Yugoslavia in 1988—just before the fall of the Berlin Wall and the beginning of Yugoslav wars. In a gymnastic hall in New Belgrade, a district emblematic of the utopian architecture of socialist modernism, Sonja trains her resilient, aging body—a body as an archive.

In the Small Village, children play all day but carelessly toss their slippers at night. By morning, the slippers vanish. Their parents explain that Muca Copatarica, the Slipper Keeper Kitty, took them. The children find her in the forest, where she returns their mended slippers. Grateful, they promise to care for them better.

While helping a woman search for her birth mother, a filmmaker is drawn into her own family history, uncovering a dark cloud that has long hung over its women. Through filmmaking as both inquiry and a gesture of care, she explores whether self-authorship can rewrite inherited family narratives.

films.ot: Stallion y la Bola de Cristal
films.syn: In his dark, silent room, a secluded teenager sick with a burning desire casts a spell. As violent visions warp his reality, a bubble threatens to burst; something must break.

A journey through the images of a regime that made cinema an instrument of power. A story of communist Albania constructed exclusively through propaganda film archives and Hoxha's private film archive, in a newly created soundscape.

The weight of history becomes light in the hands of children. A group of kids becomes an interviewing team in a Budapest park, a graveyard of enormous old communist statues. Their questions and observations awaken forgotten echoes, and through playful editing, the film captures in this limited space the magnitude of a country’s past and present.

Year 2033. Two young children discover a vending machine in a ruined wasteland, only to witness a sniper kill a woman trying to take food from it. Desperate, they shadow the killer, seizing a chance to steal his supplies and his chewing gum—disrupting his grim post-kill ritual. Panicked by the broken routine, the sniper pursues them through the shattered streets. A breaking heart confrontation ensues, pitting a cold-blooded killer against the ultimate, fragile innocence of youth.

The quiet of the night and the darkness peel away as the sun finds its way over the horizon and slowly brightens the surfaces of the Institut Dr. Simo Milošević in Igalo, Montenegro. The architecture is a prism through which the changing light of the day and the position of the sun reframe the place itself in time. Quiet, repetitive physical action activates the static compositions that comprise the film and reiterates the practice of care. The focus of the film is the inhabitants of the institute seeking to heal and the workers facilitating the regimens by which they do so.

Someone inserts a VHS tape into a VCR. The tape plays, and every type of television appears on the screen, worn by time, often unrecognizable. These are Beatrice's childhood memories. Like tapes, inevitably damaged by time, so are her memories. Thus begins a journey of personal reflection, in which she relives her relationship with her ailing mother. The search is arduous, the images mix and recompose, taking on entirely new meanings. Thanks to this painful search, the director reconstructs her most intimate narrative to try to rediscover what she had lost.
After being expelled from school in his hometown, Tarik is forced to leave his single mother, Marija, and move to Novi Pazar to live with his father, Safet, and his family.

Two strange birds get to know each other over dinner. The owl, a perfect hostess, serves one course after the other. The oystercatcher is in for a long evening filled with awkward moments and unbearable silence.

A documentary crew take a pub crawl through 1990s Derry (N. Ireland), observing the young revellers who give themselves to the night while the eyes of the security forces watch on. Using video archive and still images, 'That sanity be kept' explores being young, being watched and getting drunk during a ceasefire.

When Tero became a single father, he devoted himself to raising his son Henri, building a life shaped by everyday routines and deep affection. Their bond seems unbreakable until Henri decides to move in with his girlfriend and asks for the family home. Forced to confront his dependence on their shared life, Tero must learn to let go. The Beauty of Errors is a touching story about family, love, and change.

A filmmaker and her exiled father return to his forgotten village in Kosova. By collectively recreating his childhood memories, imagination uncover hidden war truths but also brings back to life the remembrance of fragile moments of joy.

In a smog-choked village, a retired professor faces despair when his cow delivers a stillborn calf. Abandoned by his farmhand, he reluctantly turns to the forbidden ritual of crafting a life-like calf doll from the stillborn’s body, despite his wife’s warnings. Together, they struggle between tradition and change as the quiet rhythms of rural life collapse around them slowly under the weight of modernisation.

In the early 20th century, Dutch colonialists transformed Sumatra’s rainforests into vast rubber plantations, where workers lived under conditions resembling slavery. The sexual exploitation of women became part of the system, creating a racial paradox and a silence passed down through generations. Through archival and contemporary footage, the film explores layers of memory, recognition, and resistance surrounding this hidden history.

The life of the revered 18th-century Armenian poet and musician Sayat-Nova. Portraying events in the life of the artist from childhood up to his death, the movie addresses in particular his relationships with women, including his muse. The production tells Sayat-Nova’s dramatic story by using both his poems and largely still camerawork, creating a work hailed as revolutionary by Mikhail Vartanov.

In their most vulnerable positions, women reveal deep connections between the mind and body that are at once both fragile and infinitely strong. Filmed at a Serbian Women's Clinic, a quietly powerful narrative echoing the female heartbeat, from first breath to last.

The Dollhouse is an unfolding paper world where 9-year-old Juniper untangles feelings of guilt around how her family treated Magnolia, a woman who came from far away to work as a cleaner in their house. This animated interactive VR tale explores how power dynamics are born within the intimacy of our homes. While reenacting memories with her dolls, Juniper grows ashamed of her actions and finds the courage to disagree with her parents and follow her heart. Will you help her ask for forgiveness?

THE DREAM & THE LIE is a feature-length multi-screen film that examines universal themes of art, ideology and power through a rarely-seen Cold War film archive. With echoes of history resonating today, this captivating film breaks the narratives of propagandistic storylines with a truly unique approach.

High in Bulgaria’s Rhodope Mountains, the village of Ribnovo transforms each winter for a centuries-old Pomak wedding ritual. Centred on the mesmerising transformation of the Gelina, a bride whose face is painted into a sequined mask, this documentary unfolds through a weekend, where the collective village is the protagonist. Archiving a marginalised Slavic-Muslim community in the face of modernism, it reveals a village undergoing a profound rite of passage that mirrors the bride's own.
Some forest animals secretly collect abandoned bike parts with the intention of building vehicles that fit their size. A great race is preparing. Autumn’s Last Day’s Race.

Brian challenges the religious homophobia of Belfast’s street preachers while questioning his own faith and activism to reconcile his queer identity with his religious beliefs. This documentary explores his fight for acceptance, love, and equality in a country grappling with tradition and change.

films.t: The New Policy Regarding Homeless Asylum Seekers
films.syn: Dublin, June 2024: thousands of men seeking asylum in Ireland are homeless. Olivia and her group of volunteers are trying to find safe locations where the men can sleep each night, but the government is actively enforcing its new policy against homeless encampments, and the far-right are lurking.

The Other Spring follows a young woman’s return to her hometown decades after a destructive flood, where spectral encounters draw her into the town’s layered past. Drawing together historical and imagined worlds, the film meditates on remembering, storytelling and filmmaking as intertwined acts of interpretation.

THE PERVERT'S GUIDE TO CINEMA takes the viewer on an exhilarating ride through some of the greatest movies ever made. Serving as presenter and guide is the charismatic Slavoj Zizek, the Slovenian philosopher and psychoanalyst. With his engaging and passionate approach to thinking, Zizek delves into the hidden language of cinema, uncovering what movies can tell us about ourselves.

With a deeply personal touch and an unique access, Emmy Award-winning director Maryam Ebrahimi captures the hopes and dreams of a group of Kurdish guerrillas. Once celebrated as global heroes in the war against ISIS, they now find themself abandoned by their allies. The Phantom Pain of Rojava is a post-war story set in Rojava, an autonomous Kurdish region in northern Syria, where Ebrahimi follows four friends in a house for wounded soldiers over the course of five years.

A 21stcentury Western: Nomads face the significance of a large renewable energy plant being built in central Morocco as part of a “green” gold rush. Set deep within the vast desert interior, an epic tale slowly unfolds as the need for many is set against ancient livelihoods of a few.

Did you know that the living room is actually a racetrack? And that there’s a scary cave under the sofa? Dad asks Mathilde (5) to tidy up her toy cars. They are having guests, and everyone must do their part. But tidying isn't exactly Mathilde’s favorite thing. Luckily her two tiny imaginary friends appear. Together, they ready-set-go a tidy up race – and that’s when things get wild!

Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.
To a lively tune, blossoms unfold, eggs and chicks fly, the sun goes up and down, until everything starts all over again. Everything goes round and round in this mini film about the cycle of life.

From the creator of the groundbreaking The Story of Film: A New Generation and Women Make Film, Cousins turns his essayist's eye to a decade of seismic change, exploring how filmmakers met civil rights marches, anti-war movements and countercultural revolt with new tools, new urgency and a new visual language. Encompassing landmark works and hidden treasures, it reveals how documentary has helped us see and make sense of our world.

The film-maker and critic traces a decade of documentaries, from the fall of the Berlin Wall to Michael Moore, via Klaus Barbie and The Wombles. The unmistakable film-making voice of documentary-maker and critic Mark Cousins is raised again, to educate, to intrigue, to challenge. His histories of the movies are invitations to a seance, a chance to participate in the kind of ecstatic trance or dream-state that Cousins himself goes into, almost free-associating from film to film but with an overarching but discreetly emphasised theme – or maybe motif – and always with something shrewd, pertinent and humane to say.

Nikola, a farmer grappling with the harsh reality of new economic policies, is unable to sell his land or crops. When his family leaves in search of a better life abroad, he takes a job as a landfill attendant, where he encounters the injured white stork Silyan. As Nikola nurses the bird back to health, an unlikely bond forms between man and animal.

In the heart of Ljubljana, the Workers' Advocacy Office (Delavska svetovalnica) stands as a beacon of hope for society’s most vulnerable: working men and women, the unemployed, the disabled, pensioners, and migrants. Far surpassing the traditional boundaries of union work, this extraordinary organization fosters solidarity, champions justice, and envisions a more equitable future for the working class.

January 29, 2024. Red Crescent volunteers receive an emergency call. A 6-year- old girl is trapped in a car under fire in Gaza, pleading for rescue. While trying to keep her on the line, they do everything they can to get an ambulance to her. Her name was Hind Rajab.

films.t: The Weary Hours Of Two Lab Assistants
films.syn: At midnight, two lab assistants study an unknown substance using machines and procedures that are unclear to us. Moving from analysis to foresight, the two women imagine another method of knowing; a space where rational inquiry and intuitive perception coexist.

THIRD WORLD is more than a documentary about Haustor, the legendary Zagreb band that shaped the music scene of former Yugoslavia. It is the story of two creative opposites: Darko Rundek and Srđan Sacher. Through insightful observations, a studio reunion, and vivid archival material, the film reveals how their shared fascination with the magic of everyday life once brought these two creative worlds together to create a third.

Exploring the power that comes with language itself, the worth of the device, not the meaning, an artist considers the actual price of emigrating into a “better life”, while working in a restrictive political climate.

As Iceland’s glaciers melt, poet and author Andri Snær Magnason creates a cinematic time capsule to preserve a disappearing world. Drawing on personal archives, family photographs, films, songs and folktales, he weaves together the story of his family and homeland. Directed by Sara Dosa, TIME AND WATER is a reflection on memory, belonging and what it means to live through a time of profound environmental change.

A voice drifts through water, air, and memory. Family images surface and repeat: a father swimming, animals rising for breath, a child suspended between swimming and flying. Words return, hesitate, and return again, searching for a way through breath and language, towards where to breathe.

Traces follows Iryna Dowhan as she documents the stories of women affected by war and violence. Through survivors’ testimonies, the film creates a space for healing, solidarity and hope. Avoiding direct depictions of violence, it focuses on the visible and hidden traces carried by six women, exploring resilience, courage and mutual support in the aftermath of conflict.

Mira, a film producer, is exhausted by the complicated process as the shooting comes to an end. While wandering around the set, she encounters crew members who overwhelm her with problems that have no easy solutions. She is especially drawn to the melody only she can hear, which leads her to walk through the forest near the set. The shooting wraps up, and Mira decides to leave the film.

films.t: TV or The Disturbance on Forest Hill Road
films.ot: TV oder Die Ruhestörung an der Waldbergstrasse
films.syn: Six-year-old Diego exceeds his screen time and ends up with square eyes. This triggers a series of mysterious phenomena, seeping through various screens in the apartment building. When police officers Kim and Mike arrive to investigate a noise complaint, they find themselves in a chaotic mix of realities and must face off against fictional threats come to life.

films.ot: Dy Jetë në Çorape të Ngushta
films.syn: An intimate portrait of Rilindje in Kosovo, where a high‑risk pregnancy brings serious health complications and costs her job due to pregnancy. Confronting the country’s under-resourced healthcare system, she and her husband look abroad for dignity, stability, and a future for their child.
After the world premiere of his film Being John Smith at the Toronto International Film Festival, an unexpected encounter in a hotel elevator makes the artist question the nature of reality.

Two vacations in one summer, that sounds cool, right? But when your parents are divorced, it’s never that simple. You’re one person, yet your life is split in two. Through the eyes of 10-year-old Xavi, we discover how bittersweet a summer with divorced parents can be. How do you embrace the new normal when your heart still longs for the way things were?

Through a series of animated art boards depicting a decaying Venice, the film unfolds like a set of postcards, capturing the mythical city's final moments of fragility.
