Blending archival footage with contemporary observations, and anchored by the story of the 1902 collapse of St Mark's Campanile, Venezia Diorama invites us to reflect on a city slowly eroding, yet suspended in time.

Alain Platel’s acclaimed dance work VSPRS blends religious music, contemporary dance and raw emotion. Inspired by Monteverdi, neurology and human behavior, the performers draw on personal experiences and studies of conditions such as autism and Tourette syndrome. Through striking imagery and a powerful score mixing baroque, jazz and Balkan influences, Sophie Fiennes captures a daring performance that explores the extremes of human emotion.

Bear wakes up scared while in a deralict environment. Bear finds the courage to go on and help his friends find solice in a world that makes it hard to exist. A story filled with hope, love and togetherness.
In a crumbling Indian town, three retired men protest machines replacing human jobs by pretending to be household appliances.

In the final years of World War II, a young soldier’s fate hangs in the balance after a battlefield incident. As a grieving mother sets out to confront him, their meeting exposes the raw and complicated truths left behind by war.

The last summer before high school is dawning and friends Garvey, Bas and Stag spend as much time together as possible on their pimped wheelie bikes. Together with bike repairman Driss and the wheelie gang they enjoy carefree ride-outs, but there is also tension in the air: after the summer Garvey and Bas will each go their own way at different high schools. While Bas is curiously looking forward to new friendships, Garvey fears losing their special bond.

films.t: When my father burned all the childhood memories I had, I needed to learn how to be happy again
films.syn: When my father burned all the childhood memories I had, I needed to learn how to be happy again is an experimental documentary that explores the director's childhood through the only two physical items that survived his parents' 2008 divorce: a single photograph from 2000 and a lone VHS tape from 2001. By delving into these fragile fragments, the film investigates a past that can no longer be clearly remembered. The lack of archival objects reflects the main character’s fragmented memories of childhood. Although he remembers very little, a certain feeling from that time has remained with him and continues to shape him today.

Qihuo’s first menstruation brings the “Changing Skirt” ceremony, a rite of passage marking her transition into womanhood. With her parents away and her grandfather gone, she and her two best friends embark on a journey to buy the skirt. Blending documentary and fiction, the film follows the girls through mountain landscapes and fleeting adventures, capturing the final moments of childhood before the responsibilities of adult life begin to take shape.

On the day of a decisive court hearing and an important wedding performance, a quiet wedding musician finds his private life exposed to public scrutiny. Accused of exploiting his marriage, he moves between the courtroom, city streets and stage, carrying the weight of judgment, loyalty, and guilt. Forced to make a restrained but irreversible decision, the film observes a man whose inner truth remains elusive, caught between devotion, dignity and loss.

Nestled by the banks of the Soča River, the village of Anhovo carries a legacy buried beneath layers of history and dust. More than 100 years ago, an asbestos cement factory was built. Through shifting wars, regimes, and borders, the factory endured. It gave people jobs and hope. But soon, it began to take their lives. Today, it is still belching smoke, as time stands still under the White Veil. The film gives voice to those silenced by progress and asks what remains when the skies clear.
Slugs have a hard time keeping up with the pace of life in the city of insects. When a financial crisis hits, the industrious bees only see one solution.

Four millennials from Belgrade, Serbia cross the U.S. in a Yugo, an old Yugoslav car once considered as the worst car ever in the United States. They travelled through 24 states from NYC to LA to find the answer: what does it mean to be the worst? Along the way, they explore their roots, meet fellow Yugo lovers, and uncover the unexpected ways a forgotten car connects two distant worlds.

directors.n: Arturo Lacal, Alex Salu, Jordi Jiménez
Charlotte Pion, Martine Janssens, Christine Flasschoen, Aurore Woller, Marie Fontaine, Catherine Le Goff
Gianluca De Serio, Massimiliano De Serio
Ken Yoffe & Ellen Weisberg, John Vo
